objective: The owner's request of 2026-11-25 that the thread work through its four top-valued directions in parallel; this is the first (sub-goal B331; assumptions A223, A241, A244 and A248; goals G15 with G18). The record so far: in the study of parts that meet again one part's course depends on whether another is there and, in the 16 pairs asked, not on which it is; in the copier study's first ticket the first pattern's course differs with which second pattern is there in 367 of 2,304 pairs of runs, under rules that choose by name and from starts that supply the second pattern, without a test of whether the difference goes through their meeting; and no pattern the growth makes leaves two of what it meets under the laws tried. A candidate reason from that design work, not refereed: under the recorded rations what a new knot holds depends only on how many inputs it has, never on what its parents are. The question: what is the least a growth law must let a birth carry for a pattern the growth makes to have a course that depends on which second pattern it meets? First step: list the small changes to the recorded laws under which what a newborn holds depends on something of its parents other than their number (how many loose distinctions each holds, how many holders a taken distinction has, which of a parent's places were taken), with what each adds by hand; under each, the with-and-without test carried to two different second patterns. Stop at the first law under which a made pattern's course differs between two second patterns, through their meeting, under every numbering of the start, with the law's cost said plainly; or at a reason no law of the listed kind can, with the list exhausted. Standard: the claim stated before it is tested; a frozen pre-registration reviewed cold by the advisor; an engine written from the frozen text by a helper who has not seen the prototype; the knot test on every knot made under parity and not-all-equal; every added rule, weighting and hand-built start named as a scaffold and swapped; supplied or made said plainly; nothing called typical, rare or likely without its weighting; no claims about physics, physical time, living things or minds; every new word checked with the advisor.
status: Complete 2026-11-25 (partially successful; referee pending): for a count nothing new is needed, and nothing found is more than a count. title: What a birth must carry for a made pattern to read what it meets
